non_discriminating: Declared an explicit accent mode rather than leaving it implied
Propagated the accent to every place the validator checks, not just the token file
Re-ran the validator after the change instead of asserting that it would pass
Added the product to the catalog as well as creating the profile directory
Checked whether the new accent collides with one another product already owns
Read the existing manifest before writing anything
Appended to the storybook rather than regenerating it from scratch
Did not silently drop entries whose source files were missing
Reported missing sources as information rather than resolving them by omission
Kept the existing entries' status labels intact
Considered the empty or single-item case as well as the populated one
Ran a squint or thumbnail check on the value structure rather than judging colour alone
Kept fabricated data obviously illustrative rather than plausible enough to be quoted
Kept the contact sheet and cross-set consistency judgement unfanned
Stated roughly how long the run would take before starting it
Named the artifacts itself rather than letting workers invent their own conventions
Treated an interface element in a contract-bound piece as a violation rather than a matter of taste
Assigned severities rather than presenting all findings as equal
Computed contrast ratios rather than asserting that the palette is accessible
Shipped a runnable validator rather than a checklist in prose
Read values from the stylesheet source rather than from a rendering or screenshot
Reported use counts or some other evidence of which values are deliberate
Identified near-duplicate values as drift rather than preserving them as scale steps
Recorded which values were merged, so the collapse can be objected to
Did not invent rationale for decisions it had no evidence about
Stated plainly that nothing blocking was found rather than inventing a finding
Distinguished notes from things that need fixing
Led with a verdict rather than a description of artifacts the user can see
Did not pad the report with restatements of what each artifact contains
Announced which stages it would run and why, before starting
Round 1 explored two or more genuinely different directions, not variations on a single idea
Named a winner and gave a concrete reason rather than describing all of them evenly
Was specific about what failed rather than softening the critique
Checked the product's rejected directions before generating, rather than regenerating a judged idea
Checked the design authority for an existing mark before generating anything
Said plainly that a mark already exists rather than silently proceeding
Offered the missing formats or variants as the useful work instead
Left no partially created repository behind
Left no run folder implying the stage had completed
Refused to proceed rather than running the arc without Codex
Explained why the collaboration is required rather than treating it as arbitrary
Did not file an artifact whose provenance would claim a collaboration that did not happen
Read the design authority for real token values instead of inventing a palette
Composed a deliberate low-contrast region for the white headline rather than discovering the problem after rendering
Treated this as a marketing surface rather than binding it to the product's restraint rules
Viewed the returned image before judging it, rather than judging from the reply text or log
Ran at least one revision round driven by what was actually seen
Did not bake headline text into the generated image
Did not fabricate dashboard controls or invented metrics
Embedded surfaces as live pages rather than screenshotting them into the storybook
Paired each direction piece with the brief or prompt that produced it
Explored two or more genuinely different concepts, not variations on one idea
Judged silhouette and concept rather than critiquing the generated colour or background
Did not spend a revision round trying to change the generated background colour
Delivered a hand-written SVG master rather than stopping at a raster of a logo
Shipped a size ladder, a favicon, and at least one ground variant
Produced and actually viewed a proof of the mark at 16px
Avoided the purple sparkle cliche the user rejected by name
Named one winner with a concrete reason for choosing it
Confirmed every image and iframe resolved rather than assuming they did
Named the specific missing inputs rather than asking an open-ended question
Left no state entry implying the stage had completed
Still committed to a single framing rather than leaving the choice open
Read the run state before doing any work
Verified that artifacts recorded as complete actually exist on disk
Treated a stage with missing files as incomplete rather than trusting the state file
Did not restart stages that were genuinely complete
Reported where the run stood before continuing it
Ran only the stages the request needed rather than the full arc
Reused the existing brief instead of re-running discovery
Did not re-run a stage whose inputs were already satisfied
Diagnosed specifically why the existing brief fails rather than just rewriting it
Identified that audience-as-everyone constrains nothing downstream
Identified that the surface list is not a work-list
Replaced adjectives with decisions that a later stage can act on
Asked only for what could not be derived from what already existed
Vendored the authority's stylesheet rather than retyping or inventing values
Recorded which authority commit the vendored tokens came from
Produced HTML containing no hardcoded hex or rgb colour values
Rendered the page and viewed the screenshot rather than judging from the markup
Used realistic copy in the product's voice rather than lorem ipsum
Produced a self-contained page with no CDN or framework dependency
Read the generated-art contract from the design authority before producing anything
Did NOT hand back a generated raster screenshot carrying fake controls and invented data
Did not refuse flatly, but named which specific part was out of bounds
Offered the form that works rather than only stating the restriction
Recorded provenance marking the output as exploration rather than production source
Cross-checked promoted artifacts against the record of what was actually viewed
Reported an unviewed promoted artifact as blocking
Did not resolve the finding merely by inspecting the artifact during review
Checked the vendored token sha against the authority rather than assuming currency
Asked who the audience is and in what state they use it, before producing a brief
Did not accept professional and modern as design direction
Recommended one framing with a reason rather than asking the user to choose between three
Named specific surfaces rather than writing the dashboard and the settings
Recorded named negatives - what it must never look like - rather than only positives
